references.text: Jesus' self-identification as 'the way, the truth, and the life' is directly linked to the claim that faith in Him grants eternal life and conquers spiritual death.
Here we find the same logic: whoever sees and believes in the Son shall have eternal life and be raised on the last day, reflecting the promise that the believer will not die eternally.
This verse expresses the same paradox: whoever hears God's word and believes has already passed from death to life and will not be judged.
John explains here that the transition from death to life occurs through love and faith, confirming that whoever does not love is in death, while the believer has eternal life.
The text confirms that eternal life is given in the Son's name, and that whoever believes in God's Son knows that he has eternal life, which is the core of Jesus' statement to Martha.
Paul links Christ's resurrection to the eternal life of believers, affirming that Christ, who was raised from the dead, no longer dies, and that believers share in this victory over death.
